description: Transfers selected projects, identified by their IDs, from your organization to another specified organization.

parameters.name: source_org_id

parameters.descriptionHtml: The Neon organization ID (source org, which currently owns the project)

project_ids.description: The list of projects ids to transfer. Maximum of 400 project ids

details.descriptionHtml: The list of projects ids to transfer. Maximum of 400 project ids

response.description: Projects successfully transferred from organization to organization

name.description:
Identifier of the unsatisfied limit. Possible values are:
- subscription_type
- projects_count
- project_region

expected.description: Required value for the limit named by `name`. Compare with `actual` to determine the shortfall.

actual.description: Current value of the named limit, which does not satisfy the required `expected` value.

limits.description: Plan limits that were not satisfied by the request.

errors.description: Transfer failed. Projects with active integrations (for example, GitHub or Vercel) cannot be transferred.
errors.descriptionHtml: Transfer failed. Projects with active integrations (for example, GitHub or Vercel) cannot be transferred.

id.description: The Neon project ID. Use as the `project_id` path parameter in other endpoints.

integration.description: Name of the external integration associated with the project.

projects.description: Projects that have the requested integration, each including the project details and associated integration metadata.

errors.description:
General Error.

The request may or may not be safe to retry, depending on the HTTP method, response status code,
and whether a response was received.

- If no response is returned from the API, a network error or timeout likely occurred.
- In some cases, the request may have reached the server and been successfully processed, but the response failed to reach the client. As a result, retrying non-idempotent requests can lead to unintended results.

The following HTTP methods are considered non-idempotent: `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `PUT`. Retrying these methods is generally **not safe**.
The following methods are considered idempotent: `GET`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. Retrying these methods is **safe** in the event of a network error or timeout.

Any request that returns a `503 Service Unavailable` response is always safe to retry.

Any request that returns a `423 Locked` response is safe to retry. `423 Locked` indicates that the resource is temporarily locked, for example, due to another operation in progress.

Unique identifier for the request, useful for debugging.
You can set this value manually by including an `X-Request-ID` header in the request. If not provided, the value will be generated automatically.
